scenes.voiceover: Nearly 300,000 H-1B renewals this year. A record. While the front door gets smaller, the back corridor is booming.
scenes.image_prompt: Record 291,542 H-1B continuing-employment approvals counter display

scenes.voiceover: New H-1B slots? Capped at 85,000. But renewals? No cap at all. Employers are keeping every worker they have.
scenes.image_prompt: Two doors: narrow capped entry vs wide open uncapped renewals

scenes.voiceover: Indians hold 72 to 75 percent of all H-1B visas. Tech, engineering, consulting — they are the backbone.
scenes.image_prompt: Data visualization showing 72-75% Indian H-1B dominance

scenes.voiceover: Each extension costs employers 2,000 to 5,000 dollars. Multiply that by 291,000 — hundreds of millions spent just to hold on.
scenes.image_prompt: Cost infographic showing $2K-$5K per extension times 291K

scenes.voiceover: But here is the trap. Every renewal keeps you working, but none of them advance your green card. The EB-2 wait for Indians? 37 years.
scenes.image_prompt: Hourglass showing 37-year EB-2 green card wait for Indians

scenes.voiceover: 65 percent of US companies say they have lost skilled foreign workers. The system is breaking for everyone.
scenes.image_prompt: Data card showing 65% of US companies lost skilled foreign workers

scenes.voiceover: Working is possible. Belonging is not. That is the paradox 500,000 Indian professionals live with every day.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian professional at crossroads between temporary and permanent status
